newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European shares hit new highs, dollar steady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European shares hit new highs, dollar steady.

text.p: Share prices in London and Frankfurt hit new highs again in early deals on Monday with investors encouraged by Friday's record-breaking trading sessions around the world.
The dollar was steady, off overnight levels but still keeping well within recent its recent ranges.

London's FTSE 100 index, Europe's largest share market, punched past its previous all-time high of 4,025.1 set on Friday to a record 4,044.3 points fifteen minutes after the start of official trade and up 19.5 points on the day.
It later touched a high of 4,046.8, before easing back.
Dealers attributed the European gains to Friday's 60-point rise on Wall Street which carried it to a new closing high of 5,992.86 following weaker than expected U.S. jobs data.

Investors worldwide cheered the data, believing it would deter the U.S. Federal Reserve from a long-feared tightening of monetary policy in the U.S. London and Frankfurt both closed at record highs on Friday.
But early trade in London was slow ahead of British industrial production data.
"The market was squeezed tightly on Wall Street and we could put on 30 points today...4,100 points (on the FTSE 100) cannot be too far away" one marketmaker said.
But others were more cautious, saying investors were becoming increasingly nervous of the market's heady altitude.

Among early movers, Shell Transport & Trading Co Plc hit a new year high after a report in the Wall Street Journal said Shell Oil and Texaco were in talks on merging their U.S. refining and marketing businesses.

German shares opened at a new high in floor trading. The the DAX index push up through 2,700 points, a gain of around 0.55 percent, after the DAX Ibis closed above that level on Friday in post-exchange trading.
French shares also opened slightly higher on Monday, but turned lower as the bourse continued its consolidation.

In currencies, the dollar retreated from tough resistance at 112 yen overnight, partly due to comments from senior officials of two of Japan's political parties calling for an increase in interest rates after the general election set for October 20.
But dealers said the impact from the comments was slight and seen more as an effort to generate votes from savers rather than a shift in monetary policy.

A senior official of Japan's Liberal Democratic Party, the biggest member of the country's ruling coalition, was quoted by a news agency earlier saying a rise in the official discount rate will probably be considered after the election.
Separately, Ichiro Ozawa, head of the main opposition party Shinshinto, also said Japan's interest rate levels must be corrected. He said the unfavourable effects of low rates were spreading.
The dollar against the yen was trading at 111.45 in early trade after slipping from a high overnight of 111.95.

"This could be an issue, but the comments by the Bank of Japan have been geared to an easy monetary policy and not wanting rates to be tightened," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.
"We still don't see higher rates in Japan and still see the authorities happy with dollar/yen at these levels."
Dealers said dollar/yen would likely have shed one or two big figures on the comments if made outside the election period.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar traded around 111.45 yen and 1.5296 marks versus Friday's late European levels of 111.55 yen and 1.5304 marks.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 9.7 points higher at 4,034.5.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 0.24 of a point lower at 2,152.27.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt opened 14.72 higher at 2,698.00.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was trading at $380 in early business after closing at $380.45 an ounce on Friday.
